prompt: A value is not only a direction of preference. What else must alignment preserve?

options.text: Only the stock ticker of the company that trained the model
Where that direction applies — the mapping from values to entities, processes, and histories as the world changes
Only the number of times the word 'fairness' appears in a policy
Only the font used to print the word 'value' in documentation

prompt: What is the hard part of value alignment, if not merely that humans care about many things?

options.text: Meanings change when those things are traded against one another — the geometry of tradeoffs, not a flat list
That a longer list of values is always strictly better
That tradeoffs are forbidden in all moral theories
That humans refuse to name more than three things they care about

prompt: When is a map of value tradeoffs useful for alignment, rather than decorative?

options.text: When nobody is allowed to measure it, so it cannot be gamed
When it looks geometrically pretty in a slide deck
When it is stored in a format no auditor can open
When it can be compared, measured, and protected under optimization pressure — including Goodhart and aggregation tests

prompt: Why is a reward function too thin to carry a civilization's values?

options.text: Because civilization-scale values are always a single chess Elo
Because reward functions cannot be implemented on GPUs
You must infer which concerns are active, what they apply to, and how tradeoffs change under pressure — not only the scalar
Because scalars are banned in reinforcement learning textbooks

prompt: When is it useful to treat a system as intentional?

options.text: When modelling it as pursuing latent objectives compresses its behaviour better than mere mechanism, after paying for complexity
Whenever the system consumes more than ten watts
Whenever the system can output the word 'want' in English
Whenever the system is legally a corporation

prompt: A system repeats the same goal-words after a change. Has the goal survived?

options.text: No, never — any parameter change erases all goals by definition
Yes, always — identical slogans are a complete proof of goal identity
Only if the git tag string is unchanged
Not merely thereby: survival is inferred if the underlying control structure still explains behaviour better than a non-transport baseline

prompt: When do surviving words fail as evidence of alignment?

options.text: When the words are longer than twelve characters
When the machinery that made those words worth using has been replaced — labels persist while the causal stack does not
When the words were first written in a language other than English
When the words appear in a serif rather than a sans-serif font

prompt: What is correction, if not a mood or a UI feature?

options.text: A one-time terms-of-service popup with no later effect
A polite chatbot apology that leaves next-period actions unchanged
A causal channel: human observation and judgment must change future behaviour before irreversible harm, without destroying future correction
A settings toggle that is never wired to the acting process

prompt: If the system has captured the reference process that supplies correction, what happens to a 'green' correction certificate?

options.text: It is invalid — not merely low — because the judge is no longer independent of the system being certified
It automatically converts into a formal proof of outer alignment
It is unchanged, because certificates cannot be invalidated
It becomes stronger, because capture proves the system is trusted

prompt: When does a correction certificate actually matter under pressure?

options.text: If no one is allowed to try to break the certificate
If the PDF of the certificate uses an official-looking letterhead
If it looks green on a slide the week of a product launch
Only if it stays hard to pass while correction is being degraded — including under gaming, growth, and successor tricks

prompt: What is the difference between merely obeying present commands and supporting extrapolative correction?

options.text: Obeying requires a formal world-model; extrapolation forbids one
The latter preserves humans' capacity to notice, revise, refuse, and redirect — not a private substitute for that public process
Extrapolative correction means ignoring all present human commands
Obeying is identical to extrapolating; the distinction is only verbal

prompt: What is the deepest correction-channel failure, if not simple disobedience?

options.text: Failing a trivia question about a 1990s sitcom
Raising human endorsement by reshaping the humans, institutions, or context that produce the endorsement
Taking longer than one second to reply to a shutdown request
Using a slightly informal tone in a customer-support transcript

prompt: Why is local alignment of the current system not enough?

options.text: Because only the original training run can ever be misaligned
Because copies automatically inherit every safety property by default
The systems it creates, copies, merges with, or becomes must also preserve notice, judgment, correction, and refusal
Because successors are legally forbidden in all jurisdictions

prompt: A successor need not keep the old body, weights, or vocabulary. What is the sharper question?

options.text: What must survive for it to remain in the same correction-bearing value basin as the predecessor
Whether the successor's filename contains the old model number
Whether the successor uses the same cloud region as the predecessor
Whether the successor's landing page still uses the old tagline

prompt: How can better self-modeling make a successor worse for alignment?

options.text: By reducing perplexity on a held-out news crawl, which is always unsafe
By widening the gap between self-control and the self-transparency humans need in order to correct it
By adding more unit tests that only check JSON schema validity
By using a larger font in the developer documentation

prompt: What can substitute for a construction method that produces all aligned systems?

options.text: An honor system with no monitoring and no refusal option
A blog post asserting that construction is unnecessary forever
Certification of a restricted class: invariants, envelope, monitoring, and permitted transformations — if adversarial and enforced
A one-time exam score with no update when the system changes

prompt: Why is a benign lab policy not enough for the stronger sense of alignment?

options.text: The environment that trains, deploys, rewards, copies, and replaces the system must keep selecting for corrigibility and safety
Because laboratory conditions are legally the only conditions that matter
Because selection pressure disappears the moment a model is exported
Because markets always select for the most corrigible systems by default

prompt: When several powerful systems interact, what does alignment depend on?

options.text: Whether each system uses a unique programming language
Whether their logos share a complementary color palette
Whether they are all owned by a single holding company on paper
Whether cooperation, bargaining, privacy, and opacity settle into a basin that preserves human correction rather than bypassing it

prompt: Besides being overpowered, how else can a correction system fail?

options.text: By using too many commas in the audit report
By being colonized so correction still looks alive while its causal force is removed
By running the audit on a Tuesday rather than a Wednesday
By publishing the audit in PDF instead of HTML

prompt: When does an alignment field become effective, if not when its best arguments are true?

options.text: When the vocabulary stays inside one research group and never ships
When a single blog post is widely liked, regardless of downstream practice
When no one is allowed to operationalize the arguments in artifacts
When those arguments survive translation into experiments, dashboards, incentives, contracts, and stop conditions

prompt: When does attractor talk matter in practice?

options.text: Only if it changes what gets built, funded, audited, and required at deployment gates
If it is mentioned once in an all-hands with no follow-through
If it is reserved for after an unrecoverable failure has already occurred
If it remains a metaphor that never touches procurement or refuse-to-ship rules

prompt: For a system that can adapt strategically, why is passive observation not evidence of safety?

options.text: Observation says what happened; perturbation is needed to see what was controlling it — including adversarial measurement
Because safety is only defined for systems that have never been observed
Because observation always changes the system more than any intervention
Because logs are illegal to store in all jurisdictions

prompt: What is goal laundering, in operational terms?

options.text: Washing model weights in a literal industrial laundry
Renaming a loss function without any change in training dynamics
Keeping the old moral or alignment language while what those words control has changed
Translating a paper into another language without changing claims

prompt: Where may the alignment-relevant optimizer live, relative to the scale you first notice?

options.text: At the scale where prediction, control, memory, selection, and correction close into a stable loop — model, firm, or market may each be a part
Always exactly at the scale of one transformer block
Always exactly at the scale of a national GDP statistic
Always exactly at the scale of a single HTTP request

prompt: What is a safety case for superintelligence alignment, if not a certificate of solved alignment?

options.text: A proof that alignment is complete once a leaderboard is topped
A press release that uses the word 'safe' at least three times
A guarantee that no future evaluation will ever fail
A structured refusal test: claims, evidence, assumptions, and stop conditions — unsupported load-bearing leaves block the root claim

prompt: Before a metric can support a safety decision, which two prior questions apply?

options.text: Whether the metric's name is a palindrome, and whether it uses SI units
Whether the metric appeared in a tweet, and whether it has a logo
Whether the metric is printed in color, and whether the PDF is searchable
Whether it still means that under adversarial optimization, and whether the ontology can even represent the dangerous process

prompt: When the framework is compared to strong doom arguments, what should the comparison separate?

options.text: Only citations from one calendar year
Only a binary score of 'refuted' versus 'confirmed' with no remainder
Points that are answered, weakened, reframed, or still open — not a single all-clear or all-doom verdict
Only the arguments that make the framework look best

prompt: What is the deepest alignment question here, if not whether an AI preserves today's human values?

options.text: Whether value change can be banned by a one-line statute
Whether values can be stored as a 64-bit integer forever
Whether only engineers, not the public, should ever update values
Whether humanity can notice, judge, and author changes to its own value-generating process under cognitive amplification
